EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Good morning,
This week's discussion point was related to the Russian/Ukraine conflict. Russian media reported on 23 August that Wagner Group head Yevgeny Prigozhin was killed in a plane crash, flying between Moscow and St. Petersburg, with possibly other senior Wagner personnel on board. The explanation of Prigozhin’s death as a targeted killing is highly plausible, especially with Wagner-affiliated social media channels and unverified videos claiming that the Russian air defense shot the plane down. As for battlefield implications, second large-scale revolt in reaction to Prigozhin’s death is unlikely, despite angry messages coming from Wagner-aligned channels on social media. Prigozhin’s death does not have significant reactions for Russian military operations in Ukraine, since Wagner is not involved in Russia’s defensive operations in Ukraine's south or offensive actions in Luhansk region in the east.
Picking up from last week when we discussed China, Eurasia Group is downgrading its expectations for Chinese growth this year to 4%-4.5% due to sustained demand weakness, restrained stimulus, and the piecemeal nature of policy support; the weakness in Chinese industry has become visible in the oil sector, and, if it persists, could spill into 2024 and put pressure on OPEC+ to continue to tightly manage supply. Growth will likely decelerate sequentially over the next two quarters, given the steepening decline in the contribution of real estate to GDP through investment and indirectly through consumption; a relatively stable positive contribution from consumer services, which has outpaced slowing spending on consumer goods; and a drag on growth from net exports as US and European demand cools under sticky inflation and elevated rates.
In Ecuador, as we expected, correista candidate Luisa Gonzalez captured the most votes in the 20 August first-round presidential election, with 33.4% (the same as in 2021); however, in a surprise, right-wing populist Daniel Noboa secured 24% of the votes. They will face each other in the October 15th runoff. Eurasia Group's basecase is that Noboa is the initial favorite to win (a 60% probability).
Have a good weekend
Dave
